key_insight: Sparse long-range power-of-two connectivity can greatly expand a variational circuit’s accessible operator space, but that extra expressibility does not automatically make the circuit easier to train or better for every task.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware with reconfigurable long-range couplings, circuit geometry itself becomes a task-dependent resource that can improve algorithm design, especially for neutral-atom and trapped-ion platforms.
method: Dynamical Lie-algebra analysis of accessible operator space
Approximate unitary-design and finite-depth expressibility/entanglement diagnostics
Comparative variational studies with and without sparse long-range coupling, plus a local-mapping scheme for hierarchical long-range Hamiltonians
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across diagnostics and example target problems, showing that enlarged expressibility from sparse long-range graphs sometimes helps but is not sufficient by itself to ensure trainability.
watch_item: Implementation gains depend on matching the coupling graph to the problem structure; added long-range connectivity can increase circuit complexity without guaranteeing optimization benefits.
paper_title: Variational Learning with Sparse Long-range Entangling Gates
